chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated that Ali ibn 'Anbasa quoted on the authority of Darim ibn Qabeesa that Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him) quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Seek goodness in the company of those with pleasant faces, for indeed their actions are more likely to be good.

key_terms.حِسَانِ الْوُجُوهِ: Pleasant or beautiful faces, indicating good character and approachability

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to seek goodness among those with pleasant faces in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the lineage of Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) back to the Prophet, emphasizes the concept of 'external indicators of internal virtue' in Shia ethics, suggesting that a pleasant countenance (husn al-makhraj) often reflects a pure heart and consistent good deeds. It serves as a practical guideline for social interaction, encouraging believers to seek out those whose demeanor invites trust and positivity, aligning with the broader Islamic principle of judging by outward appearances when inner states are unknown.
